title: Credit Suisse: Questions Still Cloud Bank Amid Spying Scandal
description: Oct.01 -- The drama surrounding Credit Suisse Group AG may not be over, even as an internal investigation exonerated Chief Executive Officer Tidjane Thiam from involvement in a corporate spying scandal that’s shaken Switzerland's financial elite. Patrick Winters reports from Zurich on "Bloomberg Surveillance."

asr.full_text: Patrick, there was quite a lot of news out this morning,. The chief executive to Gentian being exonerated,. But actually one of his key allies,. The chief operating officer, saying that he will step down. Then we had this headline saying that the investigators. Are still looking into what happened. What can you tell us more? So exactly as you say,. The chief operating officer has decided to step down,. And I think that's kind of deflated, to some extent,. This whole balloon of negative publicity,. Which has been afflicting Credit Suisse. For the last couple of weeks. Tiam's going to stay on,. But there still are some open questions. Which I don't think were really answered. At a press conference this morning. By Credit Suisse's chairman. And first of all,. It was a very short investigation. This thing only lasted one week. And some of the information. Which the investigators were looking for,. For example, some instant messages,. They were not able to find. I think that's definitely something which people are going to be asking about. They'll also be asking if TM actually knew about this,. Or how could he not have known that this surveillance operation was ordered by a direct report to him. So are we expecting this to be contained now, Patrick,. Or are we going to hear more from investigators in the coming weeks? As far as credit suites are concerned uh they are saying that the investigation is is over um. That basically they don't want to dwell too much uh on this any further they they they're saying. That the surveillance itself was wrong and they shouldn't have done it they want to draw a line. Underneath it but of course um you know it seems that the police uh are still looking into the. Death of the middleman. And the middleman was the guy who was between Credit Suisse and the. Detectives which they hired. And that could still drag on and still actually be a problem for the. Company. That hasn't gone to bed yet. Patrick, I don't want to insult anybody in Zurich or. Switzerland, but let me ask the dumb foreign question. I can do this to you with your. Master's in history out of Zurich. Real simple. What is the separation of the police power. From elite banks? I mean, how intertwined within the Zurich community are the inspectors from. The bankers? I would say, just in my humble opinion, that they're not extremely connected. And I think there is a very decent separation of powers there. I would, by contrast, say that the. Legal and financial worlds are extremely interconnected.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a Bloomberg report on unresolved questions in Credit Suisse's corporate-spying scandal and the chief operating officer's resignation. It critically reports that Credit Suisse said the surveillance was wrong and discusses reported police scrutiny related to a contractor's death, rather than presenting an audience-facing offer.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is reporting on a financial institution and a corporate investigation involving executive conduct and resignation. This supports financial news and analysis rather than a scam mechanism or an audience-facing solicitation.
